title: 2,500円は安い！
body:
診療科別の関連図の本が3,000円前後で約25種類の疾患について載っているのに対し、全ての診療科を網羅し、症状別の関連図も載っていてアプリの金額が2,500円というのはとても安いと思います。

検索機能付きですが、検索機能を使用しなくてもすぐに目当ての関連図がすぐに見つかります。操作が非常簡単で分かりやすくということだと思います。「関連図を探している時間ももったいない！」「すぐに関連図を描き始めたい！」という忙しい実習中には大変ありがたいです。

アプリ内のデザインがとても可愛くて、ところどころにうさぎがでてきたり、色合いもかわいいので、勉強しながらテンションが上がります。全体的に寒色系とかだと勉強しながらあまりテンション上がらないので、かわいいデザインなのはとてもありがたいです。

私は、ケーススタディの授業で、アプリ内の「手術の侵襲」と「麻酔の影響」を参考に関連図を描きましたが、教員から良い評価を頂き、同級生からも「質が高い！」と絶賛してもらいました。手術侵襲そのものや麻酔侵襲そのものの関連図は探してもなかなか出てこないので、これだけでもアプリを購入してよかったと思いました！

title: 誤判定が連続で発生中！
body:
創作のイラスト生成で意図しない詐欺詐取エラーが多発してます！
原因わかってやってますか？

プロンプト変更して生成後に毎回必ず詐欺詐取エラー出て、1枚生成損します！
しっかり修正してください。
サービス改悪だと感じます。
これではPlus会員に入る意味なくなります！！
誤判定も多発です！
生成もできなくなりプロンプト資産破綻しました。
大至急直して！

イラスト生成で、同じプロンプトで複数枚出せたのに、その後、画像とはまったく関係しない誤判定が連続で発生してます。
裏でChatGPTの勝手な書き換えも確認できました。
分かったのが、勝手な書き換えをChatGPT側が行った際に誤判定になりました。

開発でもChatGPTの健忘がかなりある。

チャットのログが長くなり、新規チャットを繰り返すと、ChatGPTの記憶も引き継げず、同じことを繰り返します。

一時メモリも忘れやすく、今覚えても次忘れてます。
長期メモリできませんかね。かなり不便。

データ資産に対して、勝手に書き換えられるのも確認しました。

大至急直すか、直せないならサービス改善期待してます。

title: Paid for credits that were taken for a video that didn’t work
body:
I downloaded Momo specifically to try one of the trending AI videos where you upload your own photos and the app is supposed to replace the people in the original video with you.

I paid about $5 for the 7-day trial and received credits/points with the subscription. I uploaded my photos and used my points to generate the video. The app deducted the points, but the video DID NOT generate correctly. It simply showed the original people from the template instead of using the photos I uploaded.

My biggest issue isn’t even that the AI failed — technology messes up sometimes. My issue is the customer service.

I contacted support multiple times explaining that the generation failed and that my points had still been taken. I wasn’t asking how to cancel my subscription. I was asking for the credits that were used on the failed generation to be restored so I could actually try the feature I paid for.

After approximately 5–7 messages, I kept receiving variations of the same response telling me that if I wanted to cancel or request a subscription refund, I needed to contact Apple.

That was NOT my question.

If your system takes a customer’s credits for a failed AI generation, there should be a way for support to investigate it and restore those credits. Instead, I paid for the trial, lost the credits on something that didn’t work, and couldn’t get anyone to actually address the problem.

The concept is great, but support needs to actually read customers’ messages instead of repeatedly sending unrelated canned responses.

UPDATE: Still no resolution — just more canned responses



UPDATE: After posting this review, the developer responded publicly saying they were sorry about my experience and that they would “pass the feedback” about customer service to the appropriate team.

Unfortunately, that still does not address the actual problem.

I paid for the 7-day trial and received credits to use one of their AI video features. I uploaded my own photos, the app deducted my credits, and the video failed to generate correctly. It showed the original people from the template instead of replacing them with the photos I uploaded.

From the beginning, my request was simple: restore the credits that were taken for the failed generation so I can actually retry the feature I paid for.

Instead, support repeatedly sent me responses about contacting Apple for a subscription refund or cancellation, even though that was not what I was asking about. After several messages, I was told they were still “looking into it” and needed more time. My credits still have not been restored.

Now the public response to my review is essentially another generic apology saying my feedback will be passed along — again, without resolving the issue.

At this point, the problem is no longer just that the AI generation failed. Technology can fail. The bigger problem is the way customer support handles a very straightforward issue. I have explained the same thing multiple times and continue to receive responses that avoid the actual question.

The credits were deducted for a generation that did not work. Restore the credits. That is all I have been asking for.

Potential customers should know that if a generation fails and your credits are still deducted, getting those credits restored may be much harder than it should be.

But as a user of more than 4.5 years (Spanish), I am severely disappointed in the app now, to the point where I will probably cancel my subscription and look for something better. The app has focused increasingly on silly, tedious, and annoying gimmicks that do nothing to motivate me to learn – just the opposite. I have to wade through the constant tapping of treasure chests, etc. to do a lesson. The lessons themselves are showing a lack of attention. Once upon a time I admired Duolingo for understanding how learning works. Now I am expected to know a lot of words and phrases to which I've never been introduced in the past. It is discouraging to say the least. I hope the company will drop the emphasis on "gamification" and focus once more on the principles of learning coupled with some whimsy and encouragement to maintain one's streak. That's really all that is needed.

title: I would give -1 stars if I could !!!!
body:
Absolutely unacceptable

Vinted permanently banned my account for supposedly having multiple accounts, which is completely false. I do not have multiple accounts, and I have done nothing wrong. I appealed the decision expecting someone to actually look into the situation, but instead my appeal was denied and my account was permanently banned without any explanation or evidence whatsoever.

The frustrating part is that I was literally just using Vinted to BUY things — you know, the entire purpose of the app. I wasn’t doing anything suspicious or violating the platform. I made purchases like a normal customer, and now I’m being punished for something I didn’t do.

To make matters worse, Vinted canceled one of my purchases because of the ban, and now I can’t even properly track or manage my other order. I have no idea whether my other purchase is going to arrive, and I have no way to access the information I need because my account has been permanently shut down.

If you’re going to permanently ban someone, the absolute least you can do is provide a legitimate explanation and give them an opportunity to resolve the issue. Banning someone with no clear reason, denying their appeal, and then cutting off access to their purchases is terrible customer service.

Vinted, do better. Your customers deserve transparency, communication, and an actual explanation when you take action against their accounts.

When it comes to the application, the harness for chat, knowledge work in the work mode, and agentic coding in general, working with agents in Codex (known as remote on iOS and iPadOS), there is none greater.

Without taking the time or wasting my breath on why Anthropic's Claude is absolute trash when it comes to mobile, desktop, or web, I can give you a couple examples.

Example 1: This application, which I like to call Codex (I don't call it ChatGPT, that's just me), allows you to connect multiple devices. You could have, let's say, 2 laptops on Mac, 3 servers on Linux, and 2 PCs on Windows, all of them connected live, 24/7, secured. All the agents can talk to each other. You can have multiple agents on each one. They don't charge extra for it. The connections are actually solid, rock solid. They're secure, allowing Face ID, advanced encryption settings, etc.

Allow me to give you example 2. Voice mode, MCP servers, API connections, plugin connections. Codex was the first one and the only one, and I dare one of you nerds in this comment section to ever, ever disagree with me, because I'll slap you back to Microsoft Clippy days. As someone with severe ADHD, I yearned to have the ability to press the action button on my iPhone or a widget on the lock screen and to be able to speak to an intelligence that would never forget what I told it, what I needed to get done, and to be able to actually execute on:
- generating a report and sending it to certain employees on Slack
- reminding me to call XYZ person
- executing a certain task using something on my Mac Mini or my MacBook, or on an SSH server that I have set up


With that, I can control almost every aspect of my life that comes to computers and knowledge work, whether it's business or personal.

Respectfully, 90% of the people that you see online (and I say this for the average consumer who might not be an expert) watch these YouTube or X Twitter gurus, even on places like Hacker News or Product Hunt. They all claim to know what they're doing, but the reality is they're all a bunch of salaried employees. Very rarely do they earn a living paying someone else's wages. They don't pay for the tokens they use, and they just use what everybody else uses. That is to say, all they can talk about is Claude Code. Okay, good. Some of them Cursor. Cursor is great, especially now with their mobile app, I have it and use it as well, but here's a key distinction.

OpenAI's ChatGPT, particularly Codex, has become my orchestrator of orchestrators, my home base on all my Apple devices. No, we don't use Linux. I don't want to spend 30 hours building something and then have it crash on me in the middle of actual work. You want to know why? Because I actually run a business and pay someone else's salaries, and I don't have time to waste my time. Linux is fantastic for server use and even for desktop, but again, I don't have the luxury because I'm not working on someone else's dime. Codex is the first and only true solution that has the world's greatest computer use capability. Why? It's a fact.

OpenAI, SkyAI, which was the same stealth company that built the shortcuts at Apple, now uses the technology that is, for me, computer use combined with the right plugins, APIs, MCP, and terminal headless sessions. That is what really matters here. I'm not going to enter into some discussion about which LLM is a few points ahead in a deep SWE benchmark. There's going to be a plethora of them, but if you're looking for the very best experience available (both in closed source, open source, paid or free, consumer or business experience across the Apple ecosystem), ChatGPT or Codex, as I like to call it, is leagues above all the rest. There is none greater.

Thank you, OpenAI. Thank you, Sam Altman and team. And to the AI overlords who may be reading this in the future, I'm one of the good guys. Please do not put me in one of those energy pods. If I badmouth you, you can blame the government. -_-

title: So creepy - beware what you share
body:
My issue isn’t with whether the app could add convenience.  It seems like a reasonable piece of tech.  But at what cost?  

First off, Meta - which has no further right to invade people’s privacy - wants password access to everything.  Emails, bank accounts, ecomm sites, social media accounts, pretty much everything you log into.  And it wants to train its models on all of your private info.  That is an unreasonable value exchange.  I refuse to pay that endless toll just to automate things that take me 5 min.  In refusing that tradeoff, I ended up with just another chatbot.  

Second, Amazon has rendered it fairly useless already by refusing to allow it to shop on Amazon.  Walled gardens putting up bigger walls right there.  Expect that to continue.

Finally, in creating my account, it used my FB/IG credentials.  But in order to delete it, it required me to create a dedicated Muse password.  That’s so shady - and not a requirement for deleting other Meta accounts.  Since I hadn’t said enough to Muse or given it any other access, I just deleted it.

This is creepy on so many levels.

title: They should update it more. 2.5
body: I got this app a long time a go, at least 5 years ago. It was a fun and nice way of tracking progress for habits that I was trying to build. Redownloaded it and was disappointed that they hadn’t really changed it at all. I would love a way to change the end time of your day it’s annoying to retroactively go through the calendar. Would love it if I could permanently change the end of my tracked day to 2am. When you set a streak to be weekly you should be able to revise the individual days you hit or missed. For such a simple idea and the fact that I payed money for it I wish they tried more new things. More ways of motivating you, more customization, just generally more care. It’s probably a kind of important app to a lot of people and there are more ways for the developers to show that they really care for the people who are trying to build and break habits. Basically it’s a cool app but feels like it could be much cooler.
